verdicts.title: Nine near-identical 'preserve file records for unowned names' functions with drifted guards
verdicts.note: Opened records.go:265-559 and manage.go:2591/2737/2767. Seven hubTOML*Tables call ownedRecordNames; RecordTables (:265), the receipts table (:354) and manage.go:2591 inline the owner loop. Carried-wins guard is present in Staged/Remnant/Attempt/StoreSync/MirrorCommit and absent in Receipt (:354), Tombstone (:411) and PrunedReceipt (:436); the finding missed Tombstone. Owner keys genuinely differ (scope.Name, name, remnant.Host, attempt via remnant), so the generic needs an ownerOf func. MirrorCommit (manage.go:2767) is generation-derived with no dropped set, so keep it out of the generic helper or give it its own small path.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Add generic preserveUnowned[V](out, fileSection, ownerOf, owned, dropped) with the carried/owned/dropped skips; convert Receipt, Tombstone, PrunedReceipt, Staged, Remnant, Attempt, StoreSync to it; use ownedRecordNames in RecordTables and manage.go:2591; leave MirrorCommit's generation derivation as is. Write the table test first (file-only unowned kept, owned not resurrected, dropped not resurrected, carried wins) and run it against current code to expose the Receipt/Tombstone/PrunedReceipt gap.

verdicts.title: Adding a record kind touches ~38 sites in 6 files
verdicts.note: hostTOMLRecords (tombstones.go:116-157) has 8 record maps (highWater, receipts, tombstones, prunedReceipts, remnants, stagedReceipts, attempts, storeSync) plus 7 dropped* sets and raisedHighWater (finding said 8 dropped). recordsSnapshot (record_pruning.go:27) and nonNilRecords (:50) re-list every field. My grep of the cited pattern outside tests gives 38 hits. Config (config.go) carries its own per-kind fields, which the plan should mention.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: As proposed (recordSet[V] with live+dropped, single records value in hostStore, delete per-kind set*/Snapshot and nonNilRecords), plus decide how Config's per-kind fields map onto it. Round-trip test over every kind first. Land after finding 1.

verdicts.title: AddResult/UpdateResult/RemoveResult triplicate admission preamble and unlock by hand

But the 57 Unlock / 19 Lock figures are summed across all app_host_*.go: mutations.go has 33 Unlock and 5 Lock, teardown_ops 11/5, commit 5/2, manage 5/4. They are not all in the three functions.

verdicts.title: Two parallel seam sets for the same dependency: SSH manager plus 12 function fields
verdicts.note: 15 '(tests, embedders)' comments confirmed. Back-fill blocks 'm.cfg.X == nil && manager != nil' number 7 (manage.go:1469,1501,1522,1528,1534,1537,1550), not 6. hostRow does branch on manager at manage.go:2167-2170 (finding said hostRow; same attachedClient call in both arms is real). main.go:747-767 derives closures from sshManager as claimed. Caveat: introducing hostChannels with one production implementer is a single-impl interface, which this repo's rules disfavor unless tests really need the fake, and it is a design choice for Jesse.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Discuss with Jesse first. Cheaper first step: delete the back-fill blocks and nil branches for fields main.go always sets, and drop the function fields that duplicate manager methods; only then decide if an interface is needed.

verdicts.title: Legacy hub.hosts.json sidecar migration and poisoned-store machinery
verdicts.note: Sidecar introduced d66d970556 (2026-09-20), retired in 3ffeccc893 (2026-09-26). Stronger than the finding says: every tag containing the introduction also contains the retirement (comm of git tag --contains is empty), first in v0.2.0 (2026-09-28), so no released build ever wrote hub.hosts.json; only main snapshots between 9/20 and 9/26 could. Tags reach v0.3.16, not v0.3.9. store.poison() is called only at manage.go:1628 (migration failure) plus one test injection, so loadErr/poison/poisoned (manage.go:398-614, checks at 1720/1769/3006) exist solely for migration. Still compat removal, needs Jesse's approval.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Ask Jesse; present the evidence that no tagged release could have produced a sidecar. If approved, delete as listed including poison/poisoned/loadErr and their three guard sites.

verdicts.title: Production-unused wrappers: TOML writer chain and Add/Update/Remove adapters
verdicts.note: writeHubTOMLHosts and ...Marked have no non-test callers; ...Known is called only by Marked. Add (manage.go:2434), Update (mutations.go:1172), Remove (:1186) and committedHostRow have no non-test callers; the handlers call *Result. committedRow is still used by Update/Remove adapters and tests, so it moves to _test.go only after those go. About 102 test call sites use m.Add(/.Update(ctx/.Remove(ctx.

verdicts.title: Atomic temp-file/fsync/rename procedure copy-pasted twice in the slice
verdicts.note: writeHubTOMLHostsRecords tail (manage.go ~911-955) and hubTOMLReplaceWithBytes (:2907) are the same MkdirAll/CreateTemp/Chmod/Write/Sync/Close/Rename/dir-sync sequence. fsdurability.go holds only SyncUnsupported. Other atomic writers exist in running.go, hostops/quarantine.go, hubcore/state_file.go (afero-based), plugins/atomic.go, transcriptindex, evener-dev; several use afero or other fault seams, so a shared helper will not drop in for all of them.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Do the in-slice extraction only; leave other-package copies as a journaled follow-up since they use different fs abstractions.

verdicts.title: 36% of lines are comments that narrate history or restate spec text; round-numbered test files

But not all long comments are slop: credentials.go:263-296 documents a real fail-closed security tradeoff and should be trimmed, not gutted. The -1500 line target is optimistic.

verdicts.title: Hand-rolled percent codec for persisted receipt keys
verdicts.note: receipts.go:239-300 (~60 lines) is unreserved-set percent encoding, uppercase hex; parseHostReceiptScopedKey re-encodes and compares (:215). url.QueryEscape leaves A-Za-z0-9-_.~ unescaped and encodes space as +, so the proposed replace works, but keys are persisted so the golden test is mandatory and the gain is about 50 lines.
verdicts.revised_fix_plan: Golden test over the current encoder's output first; replace only if byte-identical, else drop.
